new_categories.label: terminal_dry_bulk_transfer_service_readiness
new_categories.memory: Terminal dry-bulk transfer-equipment/path assurance is a delivered ship-shore service-state distinct from generic berth availability, terminal infrastructure and shipboard cargo gear.

new_categories.label: conveyor_transfer_path_readiness
new_categories.memory: A terminal conveyor or analogous continuous-transfer path can be represented as an available/degraded service path without retaining equipment type, length, capacity, rate or layout.

new_categories.label: shiploader_unloader_equipment_readiness
new_categories.memory: Shiploader or unloader readiness can be represented separately from the broader terminal path and from vessel-side cargo-space readiness without retaining model, capacity, reach or operating settings.

new_categories.label: berth_vessel_transfer_interface_confidence
new_categories.memory: Confidence in the bounded berth-to-vessel cargo-transfer interface is distinct from physical berth existence and from either terminal or ship equipment readiness alone.

new_categories.label: terminal_transfer_path_scope_confidence
new_categories.memory: Transfer assurance can be localized to a bounded berth, path segment, equipment chain or cargo-operation scope without retaining exact terminal layout or route identifiers.

new_categories.label: transfer_path_continuity_confidence
new_categories.memory: A terminal cargo-transfer path can be individually available at component level yet lack end-to-end continuity; path-continuity confidence is therefore distinct from component readiness.

new_categories.label: terminal_equipment_monitoring_indication_confidence
new_categories.memory: Monitoring or indication confidence can be represented separately from physical transfer-equipment/path readiness without retaining exact sensors, alarms, controls or displays.

new_categories.label: terminal_transfer_support_dependency_confidence
new_categories.memory: Power, control, utility, maintenance or other support-dependency confidence can degrade separately from the delivered dry-bulk transfer path without retaining exact dependency topology.

new_categories.label: alternate_transfer_path_or_equipment_confidence
new_categories.memory: An alternate path, parallel equipment chain or substitution capability can be represented abstractly without claiming a specific terminal layout or redundancy arrangement.

new_categories.label: terminal_cargo_readiness_not_transfer_path_equivalence
new_categories.memory: Cargo availability, stockyard readiness or receiving-space readiness are downstream/upstream operating states and are not equivalent to terminal transfer-equipment/path readiness.

new_categories.label: terminal_transfer_degradation_lifecycle
new_categories.memory: The transfer service can move through available, degraded, restricted, isolated, under-restoration and restored states with separate timestamps.

new_categories.label: scoped_terminal_transfer_restriction_downstream_not_root_cause
new_categories.memory: Restrictions can attach to equipment, path segment, interface, monitoring or support state, while throughput loss, berth delay, vessel waiting, rework or schedule effects do not prove the root cause.

new_categories.label: multi_timestamp_terminal_transfer_restoration
new_categories.memory: Equipment correction, support recovery, path-continuity verification, interface verification, monitoring return, cargo-flow confidence and restriction release can occur at different times.

useful_refinements.label: terminal_transfer_equipment_vs_broad_terminal_handling
useful_refinements.memory: P014 broad terminal handling and stevedoring establishes the ship-shore execution layer but does not separately model a dry-bulk continuous transfer-equipment/path service-state.

useful_refinements.label: terminal_transfer_equipment_vs_shipboard_lifting_gear
useful_refinements.memory: P087 shipboard crane/derrick/winch/hoist assurance does not establish shore-side conveyor, shiploader or unloader transfer-path readiness.

useful_refinements.label: transfer_service_vs_terminal_infrastructure_capacity
useful_refinements.memory: P021 berth/yard/land/gate infrastructure and investment capacity do not establish the current delivered transfer-equipment/path service-state.

useful_refinements.label: terminal_equipment_service_vs_generic_oem_lifecycle
useful_refinements.memory: P067 generic marine-equipment OEM/service lifecycle can support equipment provenance but does not establish terminal dry-bulk transfer-path availability or interface confidence.

duplicates.label: generic_equipment_path_monitoring_support_lifecycle
duplicates.memory: Generic equipment/path availability, monitoring, support dependency, degradation and restoration mechanics repeat prior service-state families.

duplicates.label: generic_scoped_restriction_downstream_separation
duplicates.memory: Generic scope localization, restriction/isolation, downstream-effect separation and multi-stage restoration are already campaign-wide.

stop_reason: The bounded terminal dry-bulk transfer-equipment/path questions are answered; further recall trends toward exact terminal layouts, equipment, capacities, rates, controls, interlocks, procedures, providers or incidents that are deferred to Evidence.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive terminal dry-bulk transfer-equipment/path orientation and source-discovery output; not equipment-operation, loading/unloading, maintenance, troubleshooting or emergency guidance and not proof of any exact equipment, layout, capacity, rate, control, procedure, provider, incident or current-readiness fact.
